alignments.note: The genitive relative takes *in which*; the preposition realizes the case and rides with the pronoun (rule 21's determinerless clause).
ἡμέρας is anarthrous, so the supplied determiner is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun (rule 51's anarthrous clause).

Supplied subordinator *after that* and the finite subject and auxiliary are rule 7 helpers on the participle (rule 86). Head on *commandment*: no part of *given* glosses ἐντέλλομαι, the supplied support verb licensing the frame (rules 17 and 91).
Dative article takes *the* with the case preposition riding along, headed on *the* (rules 17 and 21).
πνεύματος ἁγίου is anarthrous, so the supplied *the* belongs to the noun and not to the adjective (rules 51 and 58); discontinuous under rule 15.
*up* realizes the preverb ἀνα- and rides inside the verb's unit, headed on the verb word (rule 106).

review_notes: The supplied *the* of *the day* is given to the anarthrous noun rather than manufactured for a Greek article, no article standing in the phrase.
ἐντειλάμενος heads on *commandment* under rule 91's operational test; a head on *given* would put the head on a support verb rule 17 forbids.
